subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core own an explicitly selected FxTwitter or FxEmbed public read transport, including its privacy disclosure and long-term service compatibility contract?
rationale: The architecture and vision show that another adapter is technically coherent, but repository evidence cannot decide whether core should support and transmit user queries to this particular unauthenticated third-party service.

options.title: Approve a narrow opt-in MVP
options.body: Start with post and thread or conversation reads behind explicit mode and safe base-URL configuration, then evaluate broader endpoints after the contract proves stable.

options.title: Approve the full requested surface
options.body: Implement lookup, profiles, timelines, search, and pagination together while accepting a substantially larger compatibility and maintenance commitment.

options.title: Keep current transports only
options.body: Decline core FxTwitter support and retain archive, xurl, and bird as the supported transport strategy.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow opt-in MVP
recommendation.body: Start with post and thread or conversation reads behind explicit mode and safe base-URL configuration, then evaluate broader endpoints after the contract proves stable.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository specification identifies Peter Steinberger as product owner, and this choice changes Birdclaw’s supported transport and privacy boundary.
